::: {.assignment-intro}
This project uses Australian Bureau of Statistics leisure and time-use data to study how recreational choices differ across generations and gender. It examines active and passive pursuits, tests whether activities form a typical leisure mix, and places claims about declining reading in a broader population context.

## Key findings

- Gender gaps are strongest for some digital and social activities, but their size and direction vary by generation.
- Older cohorts participate more in several passive activities, while younger cohorts show stronger participation in active pursuits and digital games.
- Historical time-use data point to more time spent on care, work, and personal activities, alongside a decline in social and community interaction.

The analysis reshapes multiple ABS worksheets into tidy panel data and uses exploratory graphics, heat maps, correlations, and regression diagnostics to compare patterns.
